claims: On April 6, 2026, the Artemis II Orion spacecraft will make its closest approach to the Moon at approximately 7:02 p.m. EDT.
During the lunar flyby on April 6, 2026, the Artemis II Orion spacecraft's crew will pass about 4,070 miles above the lunar surface.
During the lunar flyby on April 6, 2026, the Artemis II Orion spacecraft's crew will experience a communication blackout from 6:44 p.m. to 7:25 p.m. EDT while passing behind the Moon.
Lunar observations and flyby begin at 2:45 p.m. EDT for the Artemis II lunar flyby on April 6, 2026.
Maximum distance from Earth occurs at 7:07 p.m. EDT for the Artemis II lunar flyby on April 6, 2026.
Communications re-acquired ("Earthrise") at 7:25 p.m. EDT for the Artemis II lunar flyby on April 6, 2026.
Lunar observation period ends at 9:20 p.m. EDT for the Artemis II lunar flyby on April 6, 2026.
